gen-dafont-nordic-gf-geist: Nordic spaces its tight, closed letters far apart, like brush dabs on paper, all in one monoweight stroke. Geist follows in a plain sans with wide-open shapes and no flashes of weight, so a long passage hums along quietly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-georama: Nordic feels ancient and powerful, its bars identical across the line. Its closed shapes are best at making a statement, while Georama, with its bracelet-wide c and barely rising capitals, is best at being approachable.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-gidole: Ancient brush-dab letters, pinched shut and spaced wide, make Nordic hit hard. Gidole answers with terminals apart like open scissor blades and neon-tube strokes, so the two feel like carved stone beside light.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-golos-text: Heavy, pressed-shut and ancient, Nordic stamps its letters out in a single monoweight stroke. And Golos Text, a plain sans with an x-height filling the line and a widely parted s, opens everything back up beneath it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Wire-thick and tightly closed, Nordic looks carved rather than written, with brush-dab gaps between letters. Hedvig Letters Sans runs on easily, its small letters nearly as tall as capitals and the c left clearly open, so a long passage feels friendly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-heebo: Heebo reads tall and tidy, a sans whose curves stop short instead of closing in. And Nordic, tight-mouthed and ancient with its monoweight stroke, gives that openness something heavy to push against.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-guntur: Nordic hits with brush-dab spacing and a pressed-leaf cramp in every closed letter. And Hind Guntur, a sans-serif with tall stamped-metal lowercase and wide gaps at the curve ends, sets the text at a size you can trust.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-madurai: Nordic is powerful and ancient, spaced like brush dabs. Its strongest quality is the shut-tight, monoweight heading against Hind Madurai, a plain sans whose s curves open wide and whose lowercase fills the line like capitals.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-mysuru: Powerful, pressed shut, Nordic is all monoweight stroke. Its strongest quality is the jolt against Hind Mysuru, a plain sans with lowercase tops reaching toward the ascenders and each a left ajar.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-siliguri: Ancient, tight-lipped and spaced like brush dabs, Nordic keeps its stroke monoweight. It is best at hitting hard, while Hind Siliguri, with rounds that gap like a cracked bangle and a flat gray hum, is best at settling in.
